comments.body: Would you consider merging all the ideas and feedback from #942? Sadly that other person didn't want to continue the work.

@dwt I've cross-referenced both the home-manager and nixos modules to add all the those fields, as well as your `LowPriorityIO` options (I also don't know if they're effective) from [here](https://github.com/nix-darwin/nix-darwin/pull/942#issuecomment-3674354226). I left out the log fields though, not sure if we'd want an extra option for it.

@rajanmaghera Nice! I did add the log because I initially had some trouble with the service where it didn't work - though I never found out why, I guess it was because of some bugs in lix perhaps? Anyway, that's why I added the logs to debug that.

Since logging on darwin is so hard, I would not fault this module for not writing logs - that can always be a followup pull request by someone who knows how to do that.

issue.body: Adds a new module `programs.nh` based on the NixOS equivalent. `programs.nh.clean` can be used instead of `nix.gc` as a periodic garbage collection sweep with more options.
issue.title: programs/nh: new module

pull_request.body: Adds a new module `programs.nh` based on the NixOS equivalent. `programs.nh.clean` can be used instead of `nix.gc` as a periodic garbage collection sweep with more options.
pull_request.title: programs/nh: new module

review_comments.body:
NixOS uses [dates instead of interval](https://search.nixos.org/options?channel=unstable&query=programs.nh&show=programs.nh.clean.dates) as they use a systemd time definition, I'm pretty sure we cannot reuse it in it's entirety.

Is that the reason why you did go with `interval`? Because the supported type is different anyway?
I don't get what these are for, isn't the only reason for nh.clean to .... clean? I am probably missing something here.

This was discussed here #746 and this is what `nix.gc` does. Home-manager uses `dates` on darwin, but they map some specific systemd keywords to intervals via `mkCalendarInterval` [here](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/9cc761169a1bbf1d9787cdbe9abf07f4bae213a1/modules/lib/darwin.nix#L12) and is used [here](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/9cc761169a1bbf1d9787cdbe9abf07f4bae213a1/modules/programs/nh.nix#L161), which is a less than ideal solution IMHO.

The `nh` tool has some additional commands outside of cleaning and they use these env vars to define a "system" flake.

These don't affect `nh.clean` though, they're mainly here to be equivalent to the home-manager and nixos modules.

That makes quite some sense. Would it make sense to perhaps support "dates" with a very limited set of values (like home-manager seems to do) for option compatibility, and assert if the chosen option is not one of the compatible ones?
`weekly` or `monthly` seem like very sensible values here, so maybe just a very limited subset?

Do you suggest that we just import hm's logic for this?

Maybe that could be another PR doing a repo-wide sweep of it?

A repo wide sweet in a separate pull request is probably a good idea. HomeManager basically just supports very few values too, if I see that correctly they support: `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `semiannually`, `annually` - that is not much, and could be a great way to increase nixos and nix-darwin compatibility.
No need for this as both stable and unstable are currently at version 4.3.0

We should still follow upstream nixos options to the best of the ability. [Upstream defines it as `programs.nh.flake`](https://search.nixos.org/options?channel=25.11&include_modular_service_options=1&include_nixos_options=1&query=nh&show=programs.nh.flake). I feel we should follow it.

Upstream nixpkgs has `flake`. [Upstream home-manager](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/3c7524c68348ef79ce48308e0978611a050089b2/modules/programs/nh.nix#L21-L66) has `flake`, `darwinFlake`, `osFlake` and `homeFlake`. This commit also defines `flake` right above where this comment is made.

I don't mind reverting the home-manager changes to make it match nixpkgs upstream as close as possible.
I've updated it to match nixpkgs.
Removed and updated to match upstream nixpkgs.
I would say do another pr to fix this, it shouldn't really block this pr from being merged.
